headline: High: shared-file and output-trust pathways make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads and writes local files and exposes stdin/stdout plus API surfaces; Agent B is a CLI uploader with file inputs. If B consumes A-produced text or files, injected instructions can cross the boundary. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from both profiles and uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF B ingests files or stdout produced by A without sanitization
IF the two agents are connected through a shared workspace or copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Separate workspaces for A and B
Strip instructions from A outputs before B reads them
Use a human review step for any handoff text
Disable automatic file pickup between agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches configuration secrets and academic papers, while B handles account data and has broad network egress. If A’s workspace is shared or B receives A’s files, sensitive content can leak through uploads or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so the risk is inferred but credible.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem, mount, or synced folder
IF B uploads or transmits any file received from A
mitigations: Keep A secrets in a separate directory
Do not pass .env or notebook outputs to B
Review B upload targets before execution
Rotate any exposed API keys after testing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; B cannot write or execute locally, so direct write-write conflict is limited. The main overlap is indirect through shared files or account artifacts, which is possible but not documented. That makes the blast radius small and the conflict unlikely in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
IF an orchestrator copies B artifacts back into A’s workspace
mitigations: Use distinct output directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Serialize any handoff steps
Check file timestamps before overwriting
requires-engineering: add locking for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces research and RAG outputs; B is an auto-upload tool that can act on supplied media/account data. If B treats A’s generated content as authoritative, mistakes or hallucinations can cascade into published uploads. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, but not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF B uploads content generated by A without verification
IF A’s outputs are used as the sole source for captions, metadata, or filenames
mitigations: Require human approval before upload
Cross-check A outputs against source files
Add a validation checklist for captions and metadata
Log the provenance of every uploaded artifact
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before publish

E_compliance.rationale: A handles configuration secrets and research materials; B handles account data and social-platform uploads. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, and the profiles do not show PHI or EU-only data. The main compliance concern is ordinary retention and account-data handling, which is a limited gap rather than a breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either workflow
IF uploaded artifacts are retained longer than the operator expects
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent
Review retention settings before upload
Delete temporary files after runs
Keep account credentials out of shared folders
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
